questions.prompt: Follow an agent's status change in DeskPilot from the click to the re-rendered page. Where does each step run, and how many times is the data file touched?

keyPoints.text: Rendering the ticket page alone performs five full reads and parses of the JSON file.
keyPoints.quote: five full reads and parses of the JSON file for one page view

keyPoints.text: The client picker lists targets from its own copy of the rule table, not the server's.
keyPoints.quote: lists allowed targets from its **own copy** of the rule table

keyPoints.text: The route requires a user, reads the JSON body and validates the status, answering 400 on failure.
keyPoints.quote: returning `VALIDATION_ERROR` 400 on failure

keyPoints.text: transitionTicket rejects merged tickets, returns early on an unchanged status, and checks the rule table.
keyPoints.quote: rejects merged tickets, returns early if the status is unchanged

keyPoints.text: The status write and the audit event are two separate read-modify-write cycles.
keyPoints.quote: two separate read-modify-write cycles

keyPoints.text: TransitionError maps to a 400 and anything else to a 500.
keyPoints.quote: `TransitionError` becomes `TRANSITION_ERROR` 400; anything else becomes `INTERNAL_ERROR` 500

keyPoints.text: router.refresh() re-renders the server component, repeating the page reads.
keyPoints.quote: The client calls `router.refresh()`

questions.prompt: Explain the JSON file store and the rule-table state machine: what each design buys, and what correctness it gives up.

keyPoints.text: All data lives in one JSON file seeded on first read.
keyPoints.quote: All data lives in one JSON file

keyPoints.text: The cost of the file store is correctness, not only scale.
keyPoints.quote: The cost is correctness, not just scale

keyPoints.text: Every mutation reads the whole file, changes a copy and writes the whole file back.
keyPoints.quote: every mutation reads the whole file, changes a copy, and writes the whole file back

keyPoints.text: writeDb serializes writes but not read-modify-write, so concurrent requests lose updates.
keyPoints.quote: so concurrent requests lose updates

keyPoints.text: Every status except closed can move to closed, and closed can only reopen to in_progress.
keyPoints.quote: can only reopen to `in_progress`

keyPoints.text: No rule targets open, so a ticket can never return to open.
keyPoints.quote: so a ticket can never return to `open`

keyPoints.text: A malformed JSON body escapes the envelope and surfaces as Next's default 500.
keyPoints.quote: so the client gets Next's default 500 instead of the

questions.prompt: Which parts of DeskPilot are real and which are stubs or unwired infrastructure? Separate the verified strengths from the verified weaknesses.

keyPoints.text: Beyond Next, React, TypeScript and Tailwind there are no runtime dependencies - no DB driver, auth library or test runner.
keyPoints.quote: no database driver, no Drizzle, no auth library, no test runner

keyPoints.text: Login, settings, notifications, the event stream and the worker are stubs.
keyPoints.quote: the event stream (heartbeat only)

keyPoints.text: requireUser always returns the seeded admin; there is no session or role check.
keyPoints.quote: There is no session, cookie, or role check anywhere.

keyPoints.text: docker-compose cannot build the app because the repository has no Dockerfile.
keyPoints.quote: so `docker compose up` cannot build them

keyPoints.text: The infrastructure files describe an intended future, not the running app.
keyPoints.quote: Treat these as a description of an intended future architecture, not of the running app.

keyPoints.text: Comments render as text through React, and nothing uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
keyPoints.quote: nothing uses `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`

keyPoints.text: The portal has trust-boundary problems such as a default demo token and tokens in URLs.
keyPoints.quote: Portal trust-boundary issues: default demo token, token in URLs
